exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: Propose a partnership with mutual value, a bounded pilot, and review conditions.
exampleAnswers.Working context: Common Room Studio and the fictional Side Project Circle are considering a joint workshop. The proposal starts with one session and a shared review rather than a long-term commitment.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Contribution: Preparation · Studio: Create the workshop material · Community: Gather participant questions
Contribution: Delivery · Studio: Facilitate one practical exercise · Community: Host and welcome participants
Contribution: Follow-up · Studio: Write a short recap · Community: Collect voluntary feedback
Contribution: Review · Studio: Assess effort and learning · Community: Assess member usefulness
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Why try it: The studio can learn where independent builders get stuck, while the community receives a practical session on clearer project briefs. Neither side needs to promise leads, revenue, or a permanent relationship.
Pilot boundaries: Run one ninety-minute workshop for a small group. Agree how names, recordings, and participant material may be used before the event. Each partner retains ownership of its existing material.
Continue only with evidence: After the session, compare preparation time, participation, and feedback. Decide together whether to repeat, change, or stop. Any sponsorship or payment arrangement belongs in a separately reviewed agreement.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: dossier layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
